title: Quality gates: when to break the build and when to just warn

videos.script: A gate that breaks on everything is switched off within weeks. {{red}} Nobody decides to ignore it. The build is red for things nobody can fix, so red stops meaning anything. Then one line in a review turns the gate into a decoration. {{bypass}} This lesson draws the line the whole course leans on. A check breaks the build only for what the person who pushed can fix, now. Everything else is a warning. It is counted, it is shown, and somebody owns it. {{rule}} You give the pipeline a third answer. Exit three means a warning. And a scanner that did not run breaks the build, because silence is not a pass. {{statuses}} Then you push branch after branch, and decide six cases. A dependency with a fix. One with no fix at all. A fix that has to wait, with an exception that expires. A secret pushed past the hook. A false positive. And a finding in code nobody calls. {{cases}} By the end, every verdict your pipeline prints is one you can defend. {{end}}
